claims.title: The Valdivia ceramic culture
claims.summary: On the Pacific coast the Valdivia people make fired-clay vessels and figurines among the oldest pottery in the Americas, evidence of early settled, farming village life.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-3500bce-the-valdivia-ceramic-culture, claim TL:ECU:event:3500bce:the-valdivia-ceramic-culture, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Quitu, Cara and Cañari chiefdoms
claims.summary: Highland peoples including the Quitu and Cara around Quito and the Cañari near Cuenca build farming chiefdoms linked by trade and rivalry.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1000-quitu-cara-and-canari-chiefdoms, claim TL:ECU:event:1000:quitu-cara-and-canari-chiefdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Inca advance into the northern Andes
claims.summary: Topa Inca Yupanqui begins the conquest of the Ecuadorian highlands, met by fierce resistance from the Cañari and the peoples around Quito.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1471-inca-advance-into-the-northern-andes, claim TL:ECU:event:1471:inca-advance-into-the-northern-andes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Huayna Capac completes the conquest
claims.summary: Huayna Capac extends Inca rule over all of highland Ecuador and makes Quito a northern capital of the empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1493-huayna-capac-completes-the-conquest, claim TL:ECU:event:1493:huayna-capac-completes-the-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Atahualpa defeats Huascar
claims.summary: Atahualpa's northern armies crush those of his half-brother Huascar near Cuzco, leaving him master of the Inca empire as the Spanish arrive.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1532-atahualpa-defeats-huascar, claim TL:ECU:event:1532:atahualpa-defeats-huascar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture and execution of Atahualpa
claims.summary: Seized by Pizarro at Cajamarca in November 1532 and ransomed, the last Inca emperor is tried and executed in 1533, shattering Inca authority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1533-capture-and-execution-of-atahualpa, claim TL:ECU:event:1533:capture-and-execution-of-atahualpa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish founding of Quito
claims.summary: Sebastian de Benalcazar founds San Francisco de Quito on the ruins of the Inca city burned by Rumiñahui, establishing Spanish rule over the highlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1534-spanish-founding-of-quito, claim TL:ECU:event:1534:spanish-founding-of-quito, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Real Audiencia of Quito created
claims.summary: Philip II establishes the Audiencia of Quito, a royal court and administrative district that gives the region its lasting colonial identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ecuador: From the Valdivia potters and the Quitu-Cara of the high Andes to a northern Inca capital, the Real Audiencia of Quito, the first cry of independence in 1809, the victory at Pichincha in 1822, and the separate republic born in 1830 on the line of the Equator.", terralore.co/country/ECU/chronicle#ev-1563-real-audiencia-of-quito-created, claim TL:ECU:event:1563:real-audiencia-of-quito-created, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Quito's convents produce the Escuela Quiteña, a mestizo Baroque tradition of painting and sculpture exported across colonial South America.

claims.summary: Quito criollos depose the colonial authorities and form a governing junta, one of the earliest such acts in Spanish America, earning Quito the title Luz de America.

claims.summary: An assembly in Quito separates the southern district from Gran Colombia and founds the Republic of Ecuador, with Juan Jose Flores as first president.

claims.summary: Amid financial collapse President Jamil Mahuad adopts the US dollar as Ecuador's currency, abandoning the sucre; he is ousted days later but the dollar stays.
